coverage.scope: token-visible personal repositories and organization memberships; not an administered-estate census

findings.title: CI health across the active corpus
findings.evidence: 35 of 41 active repositories have a green latest completed default-branch run; 2 have no CI at all
findings.source: REST check-runs and commit status on the default-branch head
findings.analysis: A green latest run is not evidence of correctness, only of a passing gate at that head.

findings.title: GitHub contribution activity (12 months)
findings.evidence: GitHub reports 54,609 contribution-calendar events in the last 12 months. Associated API fields report 5,306 commits, 1,811 pull requests, 58 reviews, and 1,894 issues; these fields are not an additive breakdown
findings.analysis: This is an activity count, not a count of shipped units. GitHub events vary in scope and do not establish review, merge, quality, or impact.

findings.title: Documentation density across the active corpus
findings.evidence: 41 of 41 active repositories have a README of at least 1024 bytes; 34 have a docs/ directory
findings.source: REST git-trees probe of the default branch; substantive means at least 1024 bytes
findings.analysis: A long README is not evidence the docs are accurate or current.

findings.title: Visible organization memberships
findings.evidence: GitHub returned 10 organization memberships for this account
findings.source: GitHub GraphQL user.organizations (paginated, visible to the token)
findings.analysis: Membership does not by itself establish ownership, administrative authority, or individual responsibility for every repository in an organization.

findings.title: Pull requests opened (12 months)
findings.evidence: GitHub reports 1,811 pull requests opened in the trailing 12-month collection
findings.analysis: Opened pull requests are activity events; this field does not say whether they were reviewed, mergeable, merged, distinct in scope, or created without automation.

findings.title: Visible non-fork repository corpus
findings.evidence: 60 non-fork repositories were visible across the personal account and 10 organization memberships returned by the API
findings.source: GitHub GraphQL repositories connections with isFork=false
findings.analysis: Organization repositories can include work by other contributors. Visibility does not establish individual authorship, maintenance, or operation.

findings.title: Test-suite presence across the active corpus
findings.evidence: 39 of 41 active repositories show a test signal: a tests/ or test/ directory, a *_test.py or *.test.* file, pyproject [tool.pytest], or a CI test step
findings.source: REST git-trees probe of the default branch plus workflow-file read
findings.analysis: Presence of a test suite is not evidence tests pass or cover anything.

findings.title: Primary-language breadth of the visible corpus
findings.evidence: GitHub assigns 4 distinct primary-language labels across the visible non-fork corpus — led by Python (35), TypeScript (10), HTML (8), JavaScript (3)
findings.source: Distinct repository.primaryLanguage.name values in the visible corpus
findings.analysis: A repository has one GitHub-assigned primary language. This describes the corpus and does not establish individual proficiency or authorship.

findings.title: Mapped language-layer coverage
findings.evidence: The static language map places the visible corpus in 2 layers: backend, frontend
findings.analysis: This is a corpus classification, not evidence that one person authored, shipped, or is proficient in every mapped layer.

findings.title: Account age
findings.evidence: The GitHub account was created in 2016 (9.9 years ago)
findings.analysis: Account age is not equivalent to continuous professional experience or activity.
